questions.question: Which spec should we design first?

options.label: Stream lifecycle (Recommended)
options.description: Highest risk (time, ownership, closing), and nothing covers it yet. Gives the TLA+ pattern for 6 and 8.

options.label: Read contract
options.description: Smallest step from 051 (a single instant, pre/post only). Fast, but leaves the hard part for later.

options.label: Key admission
options.description: Settles the normalization question first. Narrow, pure function, Dafny-friendly.

questions.question: Key admission: normalize or reject non-canonical input?

options.label: Reject (Recommended)
options.description: One spelling per Key, consistent with 051's exact name equality. Callers get an error for `a//b` or `./a`.

options.label: Normalize a fixed set
options.description: Friendlier for callers, but every rewrite rule creates an alias that must be proved not to merge distinct Keys.

options.label: Decide later
options.description: Mark it an open question in the admission spec and keep it out of the other specs.

Second close() on an already Closed stream?

options.label: No-op (Recommended)
options.description: Matches Python's IO convention and makes `with` blocks plus explicit close safe. SL-006 still holds: no second release.

options.label: Raise
options.description: Surfaces double-close bugs in caller code, but breaks common Python idioms.

questions.question: What happens to open streams when their session (or the store) closes?

options.label: Streams fault (Recommended)
options.description: SL-009 as drafted: defined outcome, caller still closes. No orphan reads on a dead connection.

options.label: Session waits
options.description: Session close blocks until every stream is closed. Strong ownership, but one leaked stream hangs shutdown.

options.label: Streams keep working
options.description: Each stream holds its own connection. Simple for callers, but session close no longer bounds resource use.

How should BK-457 carry the broader spec design?

options.label: Rewrite BK-457 (Recommended)
options.description: One item: 'How specs are designed'. Current content becomes one decision inside it (what a spec owes). BK-456 still follows.

options.label: Keep + new parent
options.description: BK-457 stays narrow (spec 003 symptom); a new item holds the broader design and constrains it. Two items to keep in sync.

questions.question: How many decision records should the outcome be?

options.label: One ADR + one guide (Recommended)
options.description: ADR: what a spec owes, split by kind of truth, authority per kind, Rule 3/7 amendment. Guide: skeleton, media, quality checks (changes faster than the decision).

options.label: Several ADRs
options.description: One per decision (content, split, medium, authority). Finer supersession later, but more cross-links to keep consistent.

options.label: One ADR, all in
options.description: Everything incl. skeleton and media in one ADR. Simplest now; immutable once accepted, so template tweaks need a new ADR.

answers.How should BK-457 carry the broader spec: Rewrite bk 457 but compile our work here in reasearch or rfc doc giving the right direction and foundation for the new design & adr

Which questions should the deep research cover?

options.label: Model-to-code bridges
options.description: TLA+ trace validation, model-based testing, Dafny-to-Python: maturity and cost for a Python library (decides D5's reach).

options.label: Lifecycle as checked source
options.description: State diagram vs TLA+ module as source; P language, SCXML, statechart tooling (RFC open question 2).

options.label: How formal-methods teams split specs
options.description: By component vs by property; industrial reports (tests D3).

options.label: Spec forms agents implement well
options.description: EARS, contracts, examples, spec-kit-style specs; evidence on agent accuracy (tests D1, D7).

options.description: Findings can still change D1-D8 while the RFC is Draft; the ADR waits for it.

options.label: After RFC acceptance
options.description: RFC decided on current reasoning; research only informs the ADR and guide wording.
